block:
# Notes

```mkp
note "A short note."
  requires gfx
  in msg text = "hi"
  text msg
  project md = msg
```

```note
summary: A note.
```
remark: Easy. Writing 'requires gfx' without @1 is a natural slip. My first attempt also tripped on a name collision I did not expect: an input called body (then line) is a token name, so 'text body' gave mkp.ambiguous-arg and mkp.shadow. The message does not say what a capability looks like beyond (name@N).

message: the "error" signal is reserved; every widget sends it from its error boundary (15.1)
block:
# Alerts

```mkp
alert "A message that tells the host something went wrong."
  in msg text = "oops"
  signal error {msg: text}
  text msg
  project md = msg
```

```alert
summary: An alert.
```
remark: Easy: declaring 'signal error' is a plausible thing to write. The message cites '(15.1)', a spec section number a reader cannot look up.

message: an extern has no view, state or values; providers implement it in code
block:
--- manifest.mkp ---
pack gauges@1
requires core@1
--- probe.mkp ---

  in label text = ""

message: fn twice must type its parameter x
block:
# Doubling

```mkp
doubler "Shows a number and its double."
  in n num = 2 "the number"
  fn twice(x): num = x * 2
  text "\val{twice(n)}"
  project md = format(twice(n), 0)
```

```doubler
summary: A number and its double.
```
remark: Easy to trigger, the message is clear and gives the fix pattern. Surprise: the broken fn is not registered, so every call to it adds an 'unknown-function: there is no function twice' error, and the widget also gets a misleading 'has no project md' even though one is written, which would send an author to the wrong place. Branch: only a parameter is untyped.

message: hills@1 needs gfx@1 (pixels) and has no fallback: give it an "about" text, shown where gfx@1 is missing
block:
--- hills.mkp ---
hills@1
  requires gfx@1
  canvas x=-3..3 y=-3..3 size=m label="heights from above"
    layer
      pixels (hsl(0.6 - 0.3 sin(x), 0.7, 0.5)) res=128
  project md = "Heights over $[-3, 3]^2$."
--- manifest.mkp ---
pack heights@1
requires core@1
remark: Needed a pack: in a document the header always has an about string, so the missing-about case cannot arise there (without a quoted line the header is a syntax error). The message is clear and tells what to add. Also yields a fixture complaint (no valid fixture case) unrelated to the target.

```mkp
  in prompt text "what to ask"

  column gap=s
    text prompt
    field value=entry label="your answer"
  project md = prompt + "\n\nAnswer: " + join(accept, " or ")
```

```ask

accept: [Oslo]
```

```mkp
        icon name=star tone=(if(k <= got, warn, muted))

```

--- manifest.mkp ---
pack scoreboard@1 "A made-up host that adds up the scores of every widget that offers one."
  requires core@1
  provides scored
--- scored.mkp ---
interface scored@1 "A widget whose score a host can add up."
  in of int
  signal scored {got: int}
  project md
remark: Borrowed the example 30 host pack and dropped the signal. The message lists exactly what is missing, with types: good. Several misses are joined with semicolons into one sentence.

message: "<name>" is an option of a choice here; a name can't take it, or comparing it with <name> would read this instead

remark: The 'a choice here' branch (owner is the empty string) is never reached: options are only recorded with the owning member's name.
